answer: To raise the cost of fake accounts, each identity posts a crystal shard into a bonded escrow ladder: every new alias must lock an independent shard before earning. At dawn, a random peer panel runs a velvet cross-audit that burns shards whose owners cannot re-prove distinct outbound work histories. Farming N ghosts therefore demands N separate shard bonds that survive the same dawn audit, so total cost scales linearly with the herd rather than with a single reusable key.
